attachments.title: #1124 test: add unit tests for types/state.go
attachments.text:
*Description*

`types/state.go` holds the sync resume logic — backfill chunks, incremental cursors, the CDC global position, and `state.json` serialization — but had no test coverage, unlike `resolver`, `flattener` and `catalog`.
Bugs here fail silently: a wrong answer produces no error and no log line, it just re-copies data that was already synced or skips data that was not. This PR adds *108 table-driven cases* covering every function in the file.
Tests only — *no production code is changed.*
Fixes #659
cc <https://github.com/vaibhav-datazip|@vaibhav-datazip> <https://github.com/nayanj98|@nayanj98>

*Structure*

Follows the architecture of the existing unit tests, `reformat_test.go` in particular:
• one `Test<Function>` per function under test — *all 18 functions in `state.go` map 1:1*
• a doc comment on every test function
• a flat, data-only `tests` table with `// ===== section =====` grouping and a single loop at the end
• `testify/assert` throughout, with `require` where continuing past a failure would nil-panic instead of reporting cleanly
• `t.Cleanup` restores the viper state path that the fixture overrides

*What is covered*

• *Lifecycle* — `SetType`, `isZero`, `ResetStreams`
• *Global state* — `GetGlobal` / `SetGlobal`, including that `SetGlobal(nil, streamID)` (as called from `cdc.go:65`) preserves the stored position while still tracking the stream, and that a stream set is created when the decoded global has none
• *Cursors* — `GetCursor` / `SetCursor` / `ResetCursor`: empty-key no-ops, implicit `StreamState` creation on first write, primary vs. secondary cursor reset, and that streams are keyed on *(namespace, name)* together so the same table name in two schemas does not alias
• *Chunks* — `GetChunks` / `SetChunks` / `RemoveChunk`: the deliberate `FULLREFRESH` no-op, empty-set vs. no-chunks-recorded, and `RemoveChunk`'s `-1`-on-unknown-stream vs. remaining-count contract (the `0` return is what signals backfill completion at `backfill.go:61`)
• *`HasCompletedBackfill`* — exercised down both branches, since they are different code paths: `GLOBAL` (set membership) and `STREAM` (zero chunks remaining)
• *Serialization* — `State.MarshalJSON` dropping streams with `HoldsValue == false`; `StreamState.MarshalJSON` flattening the `sync.Map`; `StreamState.UnmarshalJSON` rehydrating a chunk array into a real `*Set[Chunk]`, asserted by type assertion rather than just by length
• *Concurrency* — 240 goroutines across the `RWMutex`, verified under `-race`
• *Current-behaviour pins* — `initStreamState` leaves `StreamState.SyncMode` empty, so a freshly created stream state serializes with `"sync_mode": ""`. Pinned so that changing it is a deliberate act rather than an accident.

*Two notes for anyone writing tests against this file*

Both are documented in a comment at the top of the new file, since they cost real debugging time:
1. `State` embeds `*sync.RWMutex` — a *pointer* — so a bare `&State{}` compiles fine and then nil-panics on every locking method. Fixtures need `&State{RWMutex: &sync.RWMutex{}}`.
2. Every locking mutator — `ResetStreams`, `ResetCursor`, `SetGlobal`, `SetCursor`, `SetChunks`, `RemoveChunk` (`SetType` is the exception: it neither locks nor logs) — ends in `LogState()`, which calls `logger.Fatalf` → `os.Exit(1)` when `constants.StatePath` is unset. That kills the test binary with *no failure output at all*. It is latent, too: `LogState` returns early while `isZero()` is true, so tests pass right up until one stores real data. Fixtures point the path at a `t.TempDir()` file.

*Type of change*

• Test coverage only (no production code changed, no behaviour change)
• This change requires a documentation update

*How Has This Been Tested?*

• `go test ./types/... -count=1 -v` — 108 cases, all passing
• `go test ./types/... -race` — clean, no data races
• `make test.unit` equivalent across the root module — all packages pass
• `make olake.lint` — exit 0, no findings
• `make build` — clean
• `gofmt -l -s` and `go vet ./types/...` — clean
*Coverage of `state.go` after this PR* — every function is exercised; 15 of 18 are at 100%:

| Function                                                    | Coverage |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| initStreamState, isZero, SetType, ResetStreams, ResetCursor | 100%     |
| HasCompletedBackfill, GetGlobal, SetGlobal                  | 100%     |
| GetCursor, SetCursor                                        | 100%     |
| GetChunks, SetChunks, RemoveChunk                           | 100%     |
| State.MarshalJSON, LogWithLock                              | 100%     |
| LogState                                                    | 83.3%    |
| StreamState.MarshalJSON                                     | 88.9%    |
| StreamState.UnmarshalJSON                                   | 84.2%    |

The three partial ones are short only of branches that cannot be reached from a test:
• `LogState` — the `logger.Fatalf` → `os.Exit(1)` arm, which terminates the test binary by definition
• `StreamState.MarshalJSON` — the non-string `sync.Map` key arm, unreachable because every writer in `state.go` keys on a string
• `StreamState.UnmarshalJSON` — the two `json.Marshal`/`json.Unmarshal` error arms on a value that was just successfully decoded

*Screenshots or Recordings*

Uploading Rishyx_Shot 2026-08-18 at 12.01.07 PM.mov…

*Documentation*

• N/A (test changes only)

*Related PR's (If Any):*

None.

---

*One thing I would like a maintainer's call on*

While writing these tests I found that `RemoveChunk` does not check its type assertion:

// types/state.go:248
castedStateChunks, _ := stateChunks.(*Set[Chunk])
castedStateChunks.Remove(chunk)   // nil pointer dereference if the assertion failed

This is reachable from a malformed `state.json`. `StreamState.UnmarshalJSON` only converts `chunks` into a `Set` when the JSON value is an *array* — a state file containing `"chunks": {"min": 1, "max": 10}` leaves a `map[string]interface{}` under that key instead. `GetChunks` handles that safely (it uses the comma-ok form and returns `nil`); `RemoveChunk` panics.
`TestStreamStateUnmarshalJSON` documents the decode side of this — the case _"a chunk object is not converted into a chunk set"_ asserts that a non-array value does not become a `*Set[Chunk]` — but it deliberately stops short of calling `RemoveChunk` on it, since that would assert a panic as intended behaviour.
I raised this on the issue before starting and did not get a call either way, so *I have kept this PR tests-only*. Happy to either add a small guard here or open a separate issue for it — just let me know which you prefer.
